name: Mississippi
overview: Mississippi’s homestead system includes a regular property-tax bill credit and larger age/disability exemptions; it is not a refundable income-based renter circuit breaker.

programs.name: Regular Homestead Exemption — bill credit
programs.ageRule: Ordinary tier for eligible owners under age 65 who do not qualify for the disability tiers.
programs.maximumBenefit: Up to $300 reduction in taxes under the assessed-value table.
programs.formulaSummary: Statutory assessed-value table provides a nominal $6–$300 bill credit, split equally between school and county general-fund taxes. Actual component liabilities and shared ownership can limit relief.
programs.application: Apply to the county tax assessor January 1–April 1; reapply after relevant changes.
eligibilityNotes: Own and occupy the principal residence on January 1.
Ownership, head-of-family and state-tax compliance rules apply.
interactions: Age/disability and total-exemption tiers replace the ordinary tier.

programs.name: Age/Disability Homestead Exemption
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ or qualifying total disability as of January 1.
programs.maximumBenefit: Covered taxes on the first $7,500 of assessed value, plus the additional statutory exemption for qualifying reassessment increases. Certain qualifying veterans and survivors receive a full exemption.
programs.formulaSummary: Exempt eligible homestead value from covered property taxes under the applicable tier.
programs.application: Apply to the local assessing authority.
eligibilityNotes: Provide proof of age or qualifying disability.

Section 27-33-75(2)(c) also exempts qualifying reassessment increases above the January 1, 2018 assessed value or the January 1 value in the first exemption claim year. A subsequent lower reassessment resets that base.
The additional exemption generally excludes increases from renovations, expansions, improvements or additions, with exceptions for work that promotes energy efficiency, safety or access.

sources.title: Mississippi SOS Title 35, Part VI property-tax rules

laterChanges: HB 812 distinguishes veteran age-90 relief for 2025 claims from specified surviving-spouse additions beginning with 2026 claims.
researchNotes: No general statewide renter credit was identified in reviewed DOR materials.
The regular tier operates as a property-tax bill credit despite its exemption title; it does not provide a cash refund.
The retained SOS rulebook includes later changes. The dated enacted act establishes the 2025 table; shared-ownership ordering and low component-liability treatment remain unresolved.
